newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Frei to talk trade, education in France.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Frei to talk trade, education in France.

text.p: Chile's President Eduardo Frei left on Tuesday for a four-day official visit to France during which he will focus on improving trade, political and educational ties.
His agenda will include talks with President Jacques Chirac, a speech to the Paris Chamber of Trade and Industry as well as addresses to business seminars.
Frei's tour comes just weeks after a high-profile visit by Chirac to Latin America, including stops in Argentina and Brazil, which was aimed at boosting French trade and investment in the region.

"Every year there is more interest (in the region). In the past it was not a priority zone, but France now has two targets -- Asia and Latin America," Charles Maridor, general manager of the Franco-Chile Chamber of Commerce, said.

One of Frei's main interests is to lobby for French support for Chile's push to extend an economic and political co-operation agreement signed last year with the European Union into a full free trade treaty.
"We are seeing a very strong process of promoting closer ties between Chile and France," Maridor said.
French investments in Chile have risen steeply in recent years, although the balance in bilateral trade continues to be in Chile's favour.
"When I arrived in Chile four years ago, there were fewer than 60 French companies here and now there are 120," French ambassador Gerard Cros said.

Some of the most active groups include French wineries which have set up cellars in Chile or bought into local vintners. Other French interests in Chile include banks, insurance and tourism companies.
France is Chile's fourth largest trading partner in Europe with bilateral trade totalling nearly $1 billion in 1995.
Frei, who is accompanied by Education Minister Jose Pablo Arellano, will also sign an education co-operation agreement.
